note: Multi-turn threads for the per-turn reinforcement test. Single-turn prompts cannot test it: the hypothesis is that an appended system prompt LOSES the model's attention as a conversation grows, so the unit of measurement has to be a conversation, and the interesting statistic is the trend across turn index. Every turn is answerable from the thread itself — no tools — so the response stays pure narration. `mustMention` literals per turn are the completeness guard, same contract as verbosity-prompts.json: a turn that gets shorter by dropping them has degraded, not saved. Threads deliberately mix registers (debugging, review, planning, incident, teaching) because narration habits differ by register and a single register would measure one habit.

turns.prompt: My Node service intermittently returns 502 through nginx. Direct curl to 127.0.0.1:3010 always returns 200. The nginx location block sets `proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade";`. What is happening?
